summary: Light on a wave-swept ledge at the entrance to Lockeport Harbour, lit in 1853. The present lighthouse dates from 1948 or about 1955; it is a Coast Guard light reached only by boat.

structures.name: original tower, 1853
structures.type: square pyramidal tower with a dwelling in its lower portion
structures.note: Deteriorated beyond economical repair (Lighthouse Friends). Replaced 1948 (LF) or 1941-1960 (NSLPS).

structures.name: present lighthouse
structures.note: Built 1948 per Lighthouse Friends; NSLPS gives c.1955 and lists the tower at 39 ft (11.9 m).
Two skeletal towers placed nearby, one for the light and one for the foghorn (Lighthouse Friends).

access.note: Reached only by boat (NSLPS). Closest land view from the end of Western Head Road (Lighthouse Friends).

visit.note: Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Shelburne County shipowners petitioned for a light to mark the dangers; the government approved funds (Lighthouse Friends).
Original lighthouse completed 1853; Samuel K. Hayden first keeper (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS: year lit 1853.
Keeper Samuel K. Hayden Jr. and his wife Charlotte drowned when their rowboat capsized on the crossing to town, 28 October 1873 (Lighthouse Friends only).
New iron lantern room on a platform atop the tower, with a larger set of reflectors on flat-wick lamps (Lighthouse Friends).
Stranded on 'Gull rock, N.S.' on 20 June 1916 (the Department's year to 31 March 1917); master's certificate suspended six months. The report does not confirm that this is the Lockeport rock.
Hand fog alarm replaced by a compressed-air diaphone on 1 May 1918 (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS: fog signal established 1918.
Fourth-order dioptric lens, group occulting white every 30 seconds, with an air diaphone (NSLPS).
New two-storey lighthouse replaced the original tower (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS: replaced the 1853 tower in 1941-1960 and lit c.1955.
Athenite sprayed on the exterior walls, increasing their thickness from 30 cm to nearly 43 cm (Lighthouse Friends).
De-staffed 1987; fog-alarm building, workshop and boathouse removed (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS: automated by 1987.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record notes that sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The Coast Guard's List of Lights gives a current light (LFl W 15s). NSLPS's Gull Rock II page says 'This light is operational' but also gives 'Still Operating: No' on the same page, so the Coast Guard list is taken as current.

notes_for_editor: 1) The 1916 stranding is on 'Gull rock, N.S.' with no further detail in the OCR text; the vessel is not named in the passage read. The OCR text of scan 142 (printed p. 135) gives only 'Gull rock, N.S.' and does not place it at Lockeport; the story says so. 2) The 1873 drowning rests on Lighthouse Friends alone. A Chronicling America search for Lockeport and Hayden in 1873-74 returned no hits. A WikiTree page (not used) gives Charlotte (Freeman) Hayden's death at Gull Rock Light in 1873. 3) The Department's 1904 bell buoy is marked 'Bull rock' and sits a short distance south of it; the sources do not say whether Bull rock and Gull Rock are the same rock. The story says the report calls it Bull rock and does not equate them. Check a chart. 4) Built date conflict: Lighthouse Friends and the record say 1948; NSLPS says the replacement began about 1955 and gives a 1941-1960 span. Unresolved; the story gives both. 5) NSLPS's Gull Rock II page is internally inconsistent (operational, but 'Still Operating: No'; 'Occulting White (1990)' against the Coast Guard's LFl W 15s). 6) The 1902 keeper table (Orchard, L. D., against Gull Rock) was matched by position in OCR text (scan 245); the page image was checked: the row reads Orchard, L. D. / Gull Rock / 1, 1877 / 400 00 (printed p. 68). 7) Keepers after 1960 (Bill Ringer, Arnold Dooks, Jim Guptill, Eric A. Stevens, Barry L. Crowell, W.R.R. Murphy) are named only as Lighthouse Friends and NSLPS print their roles. Lighthouse Friends' personal details (ages, marriage, children) are left out. 8) Carter Island Light, the town's other light, is a different station; check whether a record exists before writing about it. 9) The Department's 1901-02 lists also have 'Cariboo Island or Gull Rock' and 'Gull Rock, Carribou Island'; not used, unclear identity. 10) The Lighthouse Friends page is copyrighted; the story uses facts and its own wording, with one short quotation at most per passage.
